short: The 1533 Succession to the Crown Act declared Mary illegitimate and settled the succession on Henry VIII's children by Anne Boleyn.
full:
Passed by the Reformation Parliament and given royal assent in March 1534, the First Succession Act formally severed England from papal authority over royal marriages. It declared Henry VIII's marriage to Catherine of Aragon invalid and his marriage to Anne Boleyn lawful. As a result, Princess Mary was stripped of her status as heir apparent and bastardised, and the succession was vested in the newly born Princess Elizabeth and any future children of Henry and Anne.

The Act also required all subjects, if commanded, to swear an oath recognising its provisions. Refusal to take the Oath of Succession was declared misprision of treason, a crime carrying the penalty of life imprisonment and confiscation of property. This oath became the primary mechanism for purging prominent dissenters, notably leading to the arrests of Sir Thomas More and Bishop John Fisher when they refused to swear.
